recentItems.title: China through the senses: Whisper of nature
recentItems.description:
From vast wetlands to tropical rainforests and high mountain habitats, China is home to an extraordinary diversity of life – from hundreds of thousands of migratory birds at Poyang Lake to Asian elephants in Yunnan, rare wild orchids in Hainan and the endangered Guizhou snub-nosed monkey.

Through the eyes, ears and footsteps of the people who protect them, this film explores the delicate connections between humans and the natural world – and how science, technology and steadfast stewardship are helping safeguard China's rich biodiversity.

From wetlands and mountains to tropical rainforests, these stories reveal how people and wildlife are finding a shared rhythm, protecting not only individual species but the ecosystems they call home.

Every living thing has a spirit. All life shares one rhythm.

recentItems.title: What do President Xi's recent visits reveal about China's diplomatic vision?
recentItems.description:
In just one week, Chinese President Xi Jinping attended the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek and paid state visits to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt  –  engagements that produced a series of important diplomatic outcomes.
At the SCO summit, leaders adopted the Bishkek Declaration and 28 outcome documents. In Kyrgyzstan, China and Kyrgyzstan signed a joint declaration on advancing their comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, along with a treaty on permanent good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation. In Egypt, the two sides signed cooperation documents covering trade, artificial intelligence, the digital economy and transport.
So, what are the major takeaways from these trips? And what do they tell us about China's diplomatic priorities and vision for the future?
To explore these questions, our guests in this edition of Dialogue are Wang Xinsong, associate professor at Beijing Normal University; Hisham Abubakr Metwally Mohamed, first economist researcher at Egypt's Ministry of Foreign Trade and Industry; Zoon Ahmed Khan, founder of the ShangHe Review; and Professor Kubanychbek Taabaldiev of Ala-Too International University in Kyrgyzstan.

recentItems.title: In conversation with the ancients: Drawing new life from timeless stories
recentItems.description:
What does Mulan mean to a young artist today? For Chinese artist and picture-book creator Ye Luying, she is more than a legendary warrior. 

Having grown up in a small town before pursuing her dreams in a big city, Ye sees her own journey in Mulan's: leaving home, facing uncertainty and making choices of her own.

From Nymph of the Luo River (Luoshenfu), winner of the Best Illustration Gold Award at the 13th Golden Dragon Award, to her latest picture book on Mulan, Ye continues to revisit ancient stories through a contemporary lens.

For her, creating picture books on stories dating back 1,000 years is a way of "having a conversation with the ancients," as these stories still speak to us today.

recentItems.title: The Heat: Gaza & West Bank | Military raids, settler violence
recentItems.description:
The death and destruction in Gaza continue as Israel enforces its occupation of the enclave and targets Hamas. According to Gaza’s Ministry of Health, more than 1,300 Palestinians, including over 300 children, have been killed there since a ceasefire was declared last October.
 
And, in the West Bank Israeli settler violence has escalated as more Palestinians are driven from their homes and see their properties destroyed. Meanwhile, Israel plans even more illegal settlements that some fear could kill a two-state solution. #Gaza #WestBank #settlerviolence #Israel #Palestine 

The #Heat host: Anand Naidoo 

Guests:
Shahd Hammouri is a lecturer in International Law and Legal Theory at the University of Kent.  
Xavier Abu Eid is a political scientist. 
Said Arikat is Washington correspondent for the Al Quds Daily Newspaper, and he’s an adjunct professor at American University.

recentItems.title: Gyirong mudslide reporting: Western media's familiar political script
recentItems.description:
Host Nadim Diab breaks down the unfounded allegations that China is censoring disaster coverage and that its infrastructure triggered the deadly mudslide that struck Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. He highlights how multiple media outlets have weaponized both narratives for political framing. That is not reporting a disaster; it is manipulating it.#goodpoint
